newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: One S.Korean union leader released, four still held.
newsitem.headline: One S.Korean union leader released, four still held.

text.p: Police have released a South Korean union leader arrested for obstructing business by leading work stoppages but four other unionists are still being held, a prosecution official said on Thursday.

The official also said prosecutors would soon decide on whether to drop outstanding arrest warrants for other heads of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions. The move follows President Kim Young-sam's order to suspend execution of the warrants.

The official said Kim Im-shik, a confederation leader from Hyundai Heavy Industries in the southeast city of Ulsan, was released overnight after reqesting a review of the legality of his arrest. He was arrested on Saturday.

The official said the other four, all from a shipyard run by Halla Heavy Industries, had not requested a similar review and were still being held, pending a decision by prosecutors on whether charges relating to their arrest should be dropped.

On Wednesday, police allowed confederation boss Kwon Young-kil to lead a protest march through Seoul streets after he left Myongdong Cathedral where he had been sheltering from arrest. Kwon later returned to the church.

Prosecutors have 15 arrest warrants still outstanding for confederation leaders, including Kwon and six deputies, who have been directing strikes in protest at the forced passage of a controversial labour law.
